business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Oversized Furniture and Home Decor

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between the Republic of Korea and the United States for the Avoidance of Double Taxation
Convention between the Republic of Korea and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Transaction Reports Act (FTRA) under the Financial Services Commission; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality; Commercial Act Articles 289, 291, 292 and 317; Regulation on the Registration of Beneficial Owners under the Act on the Regulation of Specified Information; Ministry of Justice decree on corporate UBO registration taking effect November 1, 2024 under the Commercial Act Amendment; Korea Customs Service regulations for e-commerce business filings.

additional_instruments_required: Identity and address proof of each UBO notarized in home jurisdiction and apostilled or legalized
Certified translation of any non-Korean corporate documents into Korean for the registry
Power of attorney granted to the Korean administrative agent
Bank account opening application with due diligence packet

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders, beneficial owners and signatories must be screened against South Korea's Financial Action Task Force-aligned watchlists, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the UK HM Treasury sanctions list, and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit's advisory notices. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any individual or entity with 25% or greater ownership or control, all politically exposed persons, and any person with adverse media or past enforcement actions. Sanctions screening must occur continuously by subscription-based automated screening tools, with a full re-screening event at onboarding, weekly interval scans, and immediate triggered re-screening upon any change in UBO or on the issuance of any new sanctions list. For cross-border e-commerce in oversized furniture, additional customer risk flagging is required if payment is routed through ransomware-prone jurisdictions or if bulk cash deposits are made in Korea. Any positive match must be reported as a suspicious transaction report to the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit within 24 hours, and no transaction may be processed without approval by the compliance officer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Supreme Court Registry Office – Internet Registration Service (인터넷등기소)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Korean corporate name must be in the Korean alphabet (Hangul) or a foreign language using Roman letters, but the statutory registry will record a Hangul transliteration for official court registration. The name must contain a distinguishing feature from all pre-existing names, and cannot consist solely of geographic terms, business type descriptions, or generic industry words. The four-tier naming convention requires: first, a unique cooperative or corporate identifier; second, an industry description matching the object clause; third, the legal form designation (“Chusik Hoesa” or “주식회사”); and fourth, no sensitive token unless approved. If using a foreign language name, a Korean phonetic transliteration must be created and cleared for conflict. English names must be accompanied by the Korean transliteration in the articles of incorporation and the registry filing. Use of Arabic, Chinese, or other non-Latin scripts without Korean transliteration will be rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name clearance application is rejected by the Korean Supreme Court Registry Office, the applicant may file a written objection with the competent district court registry within 14 days of receiving the rejection. The appeal must state the legal basis for distinctiveness, include a proposed alternative transliteration, and, where the rejection is based on alleged similarity to an existing name, provide a comparison of the Hangul spelling, pronunciation and visual impression. The court registrar will review the objection and issue a decision within 7 to 15 business days. If the registrar maintains the rejection, the applicant may appeal to the High Court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. During the appeal, no identical name may be reserved by the applicant. It is operationally recommended to simultaneously reserve a second and third backup name to avoid incorporation delay. If the rejection relates to a sensitive token, an application may be made to the relevant ministry for prior authorization, and the authorized letter must be submitted to the registry before a new application.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop_alt: Alternative administrative remedy: file a new name clearance application with a new distinctive constituent and withdraw the rejected name within 14 days to preserve the timeline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is permissible for name clearance and registration only if it includes a physical Korean address and a leased office space where corporate records and seals can be kept. However, the Korean National Tax Service and most Korean banks will reject a pure virtual mailbox for an online retailer of oversized furniture because the entity is classified as an e-commerce retailer performing continuous economic activity. The address must be a registered place of business where the tax authority can serve notices and conduct audits and where the corporate seal is physically available. A virtual office solution that provides a dedicated room, mail handling, and occasional meeting space may be accepted if the landlord issues a lease agreement in the company's name, the address is not shared with more than two other entities, and the office is accessible during business hours. For cross-border oversized freight e-commerce, a warehouse address separate from the registered office is acceptable, but the registered office still requires a physical commercial presence. If the target market is also the United States or EU, an additional brick-and-mortar office is not required in Korea, but the Korean registered office must meet the 'place of actual management' standard.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 9% annual likelihood of an unannounced municipal tax or district tax inspection for newly incorporated companies in the first two years, rising to 17% if the registered office is a shared space or virtual office. The Seoul Regional Tax Office, National Tax Service, and local gu office may visit without notice to verify the signboard, office capacity, number of employees, and availability of books and records. Checklist: (a) place a visible Korean signboard with the full corporate name; (b) maintain the corporate seal, statutory ledger, tax invoices and accounting software within the office; (c) ensure at least one director or a qualified administrative staff member is present during business hours; (d) do not instruct mail forwarding to a P.O. box for tax notices; (e) keep a physical visitor log and lease agreement on hand; (f) if running an online-only operation, document how the office is used for management and customer service; and (g) for customs and bonded warehouse activities, ensure the warehouse declarations match the business scope. If a physical inspection yields zero employees present, no business records, and no corporate signboard, the tax authority may reassess the place of effective management and impose a 2% penalty on unreported income plus delay penalties.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_office_requirement: A physical office with exclusive or semi-exclusive use is mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited virtual office acceptable if it is not a pure P.O. box; must be a serviced office with lease agreement, signage, and record-keeping capacity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 9-17% annual probability based on district, sector, and virtual-office signal.
inspection_checklist: Signboard posted at the office entrance in Korean
Lease agreement or authorized sublease with the registered address
Bookkeeping records and electronic tax invoices maintained on-site or in a domestic cloud
One or more directors or staff members can be physically present within 24 hours of a request
Customer service and order-management functions are demonstrably operated from the Korean office
If the office is shared, a dedicated partition, desk, filing cabinet, and phone line must exist

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and company register search fee before incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean Supreme Court Registry Office / Internet Registration Service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government fee: 600 KRW per search output plus 2,000 KRW per full certificate; market benchmark for professional search and clearance report is $50-120.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration duty on incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa with capital below KRW 100 million
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean Supreme Court Registry Office (stamp revenue)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registration Special Measures Act: 0.4% of capital for capital up to KRW 100 million; 20% reduction for filing online. Example capital KRW 50 million = KRW 200,000 reduced to KRW 160,000 (~USD 120-180).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization fee for Articles of Association (정관) and incorporation resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff based on capital amount; typically KRW 200,000-350,000 (~USD 150-260) for a standard incorporation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified copy of corporate registration register and seal certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: 4,000 KRW per certified copy; 5,000 KRW per seal certificate; approximately USD 3-5 per document with agent handling fees.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent or incorporation attorney professional fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Korean law firm or licensed certified administrative agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: $800-$2,000 for full incorporation, including drafting articles, obtaining business registration, opening bank account support, and name clearance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Business registration certificate issuance fee at the local tax office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official government fee; statutory free issuance of business registration certificate during incorporation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office monthly lease for a serviced office or commercial co-working unit
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Private commercial landlord / serviced office operator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: KRW 500,000-KRW 1,500,000 per month in Seoul secondary commercial zones; first month advance payment $500-$900.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Landlord deposit (one-time, refundable) treated as cash outlay
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Private commercial landlord / serviced office operator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market standard one to two months deposit; refundable. Cash outflow item not an expense for tax but budgeted for pre-incorporation liquidity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account opening assistance and compliance onboarding fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Korean banks do not charge standard account opening fees, but external accountant or lawyer assistance is $200-$500.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/UBO screening and due diligence on foreign incorporator and all 25%+ beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External compliance service provider / Korean law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: $100-$500 per name alert package, inclusive of continuous screening for 90 days.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of incorporation documents for foreign bank account opening and treaty benefits
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea / foreign embassy in Seoul
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Korean MOFA Apostille: KRW 12,000 per document (~USD 10). Consular legalization varies by embassy USD 20-$80 per document. Notary and translation additional.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of registration documents into Korean if original documents are in English/Chinese
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: KRW 20,000-35,000 per page; 5-10 pages at $20-$30 per page.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Configure email, online payment processor registration (Stripe, Affirm BNPL) and GDPR/consumer contract templates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial market fee: $500-$800 for stage-one legal setup of payment rails and e-commerce compliance templates.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 10000, as amended, Chapter II for Stock Corporations, specifically Articles 289, 292, 295, 317, 318, 329, 330, 340, 356, 383, 393 and 410
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: District Court Registry Office having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; online submission through the Supreme Court Online Registration Center at www.iros.go.kr
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa Stock Corporation together with the authentic certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation and the capital payment certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea does not impose a statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Chusik Hoesa. However, all shares subscribed at incorporation must be fully paid before registration. The subscription funds must be deposited into a dedicated blocked capital subscription escrow account maintained with a licensed financial institution in Korea in the name of the corporation under formation, and the depositary bank must issue a capital payment certificate and deposit balance confirmation that will be attached to the registration application submitted to the court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: [PROPOSED COMPANY NAME] CHUSIK HOESA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION. WHEREAS the Company has been formed under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and its incorporation registration has been prepared for filing with the competent District Court Registry Office, and WHEREAS the board of directors is vested with authority to establish the capital structure, banking arrangements, registered office and statutory offices of the Company; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the authorized share capital of the Company shall be [●] ordinary shares, with a par value of [●] Korean won per share, and that of that authorized capital, [●] shares shall be issued at incorporation and are hereby confirmed as fully paid by deposit of the aggregate subscription price into the capital subscription escrow account maintained at [●] Bank, account number [●]. The board ratifies the issuance of those shares in accordance with the shareholder register and directs the representative director to arrange for share certificates to be prepared and delivered in compliance with Articles 330, 356 and 361 of the Commercial Act. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company shall be located at [●] Street, [●] District, [●] City, Republic of Korea, within the registry jurisdiction of [●] District Court, and that such location is adopted as the Company's legal seat for statutory notices, service of process and administrative filings. The representative director is directed to execute or approve the registered office lease and to supply all address evidence required for registration. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the board authorizes the opening and operation of corporate current accounts, savings accounts, foreign currency accounts and e-commerce settlement accounts with [●] Bank, [●] branch, and with such other financial institutions as the board may approve. Any one of the representative director, the chief financial officer and the treasurer, acting jointly with at least one other approved signatory, shall have authority to open, fund, operate and close corporate accounts and to execute banking agreements in the ordinary course. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the following statutory officers are hereby appointed: [●] as representative director and chief executive officer, [●] as director responsible for finance and administration, and [●] as auditor, provided that if the Company does not meet the statutory size thresholds requiring a regular auditor, the board may appoint an audit committee or internal compliance officer with equivalent supervisory authority. Each officer shall perform the duties imposed by the Commercial Act, including the preparation of annual financial statements, the retention of books and records, the filing of statutory reports, and the implementation of licensing, tax and labor compliance. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that all lawful actions taken by the promoters and provisional officers before the date of this resolution to prepare and execute the Articles of Incorporation, open the capital escrow account, and engage professional advisers are hereby ratified and approved, and this resolution shall remain in full force until revoked by a later resolution of the board of directors. ADOPTED by unanimous consent of the initial directors on [●].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, execute and notarize the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public licensed under the Notary Public Act of the Republic of Korea; subsequent review by the competent District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a Korean-language Articles of Incorporation containing all mandatory statutory matters under Articles 289 and 292 of the Commercial Act, including the corporate purpose of online retail, distribution and warehousing of oversized furniture and home decor; the trade name; the registered office address; the total authorized shares; the par value; the shares issued at incorporation; the method of public notice; and the provisions for the board of directors and representative director. Every incorporator must execute the Articles of Incorporation before a notary public, who must verify the identity, legal capacity and free consent of each signatory. The notary must ensure that the corporate purpose is lawful and that the share structure complies with Article 329 of the Commercial Act. The notarized Articles of Incorporation must then be issued as an authentic certified copy for submission to the registry, together with any registration consents of landlords and directors.
required_dossiers: Valid passports or resident registration certificates of all incorporators
Draft Articles of Incorporation initialed on each page
Power of attorney and corporate authorization if a corporate entity acts as incorporator
Consent letter of the owner or lessor of the registered office
Registered seal certificates or notarized identity certificates of the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a formal deficiency, the incorporators may amend and re-execute the Articles of Incorporation on the same business day. If the District Court Registry later questions the notarization, the applicant may file a supplementary explanatory certificate from the notary or, if the defect is substantive, withdraw and refile the registration after correcting the Articles of Incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscribe shares and deposit paid-in capital into the blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed depositary bank in the Republic of Korea authorized to accept corporate capital subscription escrow deposits; the issuing bank is the formal provider of the capital payment certificate required under Article 295 of the Commercial Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a special capital subscription escrow account in the exact name of the corporation under formation and deposit or transfer the full amount of the subscription price for all issued shares, in cash or by wire transfer from an account of the subscribing incorporator. The bank must block any withdrawal until the corporate registration is completed, and the incorporators must obtain an original certificate of deposit indicating the corporate provisional name, amount paid, date of payment and account number. No share certificate may be delivered before registration. The incorporators must ensure that the aggregate deposit equals the full aggregate par value or issue price of the shares subscribed at incorporation, and that no contribution in kind is used without the special inspection procedures required by Articles 290 and 294 of the Commercial Act.
required_dossiers: Final authentic copy of the notarized Articles of Incorporation
Identification documents of all share subscribers
Share subscription applications or subscription ledger
Bank remittance receipt and capital payment certificate
Asset valuation or in-kind contribution inspection report if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue a capital payment certificate because of a mismatch in the corporate provisional name or the subscriber identity, the incorporators should redeposit the funds under the exactly registered provisional corporate name and obtain a corrected certificate. If the deposited sum is released prematurely, the capital deficiency may be cured only by re-depositing the full amount and submitting a new certificate before the registration application is filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitute the statutory organs and adopt the first board resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators meeting for the election of initial directors and auditor; thereafter the first board of directors meeting of the newly formed Chusik Hoesa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the incorporators meeting to elect the initial directors and auditor in accordance with Article 316 of the Commercial Act. At a stock corporation whose last fiscal year paid-in capital exceeds one billion Korean won, or whose debt exceeds two billion Korean won, the Company must appoint the statutory auditor and independent auditor required by the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies. The elected directors must then convene the first board meeting, at which they appoint the representative director, fix the registered office, approve the bank mandate, ratify the issue of shares, and appoint any other executive officers. Both the incorporators meeting minutes and the board meeting minutes must record the attendance, voting results and adopted resolutions, and must be signed or sealed by the chairman and attending directors. These minutes become essential evidence for the court registry and the corporate bank account opening process.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the incorporators meeting
Minutes of the first board of directors meeting
Capital payment certificate from the depositary bank
Written consents and proxy forms of incorporators and directors
Curriculum vitae, nationality and disqualification declarations of each director and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an elected director or auditor is disqualified under Article 382 paragraph 2 or Article 400 of the Commercial Act, the election is void and a new meeting must be convened. If the minutes are incomplete or lack signatures, supplementary minutes may be prepared and executed by all participants to cure the procedural defect before the registration filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the registration of incorporation with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registry Office of the local court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic filing through the Supreme Court Online Registration System at www.iros.go.kr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and sign the official Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation under Article 317 of the Commercial Act. Attach the certified authentic copy of the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital payment certificate, the minutes of the incorporators meeting, the minutes of the first board meeting, the consents of directors and auditor, the lease contract or ownership evidence for the registered office, and the representative's identification. Pay the registration stamp duty and the court registry fee at the designated window or through the electronic payment system. The registrar will examine whether the incorporation procedures and statutory contents are lawful. If the registrar is satisfied, the corporation is deemed incorporated as of the registration date and a Certificate of Registered Matters will be issued, enabling the release of the escrow capital and subsequent business registration steps.
required_dossiers: Signed Application for Registration of Incorporation on the official court form
Certified authentic copy of the notarized Articles of Incorporation
Original capital payment certificate from the depositary bank
Minutes of the incorporators meeting and first board meeting
Consent letters and identity documents of directors and auditor
Power of attorney for any agent filing the application
Lease contract or ownership certificate for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementary order or a suspension of registration, the applicant must file all missing documents within the prescribed statutory period, usually two weeks. If registration is refused, counsel may cure the stated defect and submit a new application; a formal refusal may also be challenged by an immediate appeal to the competent court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain business registration, file the mail-order sales report and activate corporate bank accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office; local municipal government office for the mail-order sales report under the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after commencing business, file the application for business registration of the newly incorporated Chusik Hoesa with the competent tax office, identifying the legal entity and selecting the applicable business codes for online retail, import or storage of oversized furniture. Attach the corporate registration extract, certified Articles of Incorporation, lease agreement, and the representative director's identity credential. Obtain the Business Registration Certificate together with VAT reporting credentials. Independently submit the mail-order sales business report to the local municipal government in accordance with Article 12 of the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce. If the Company maintains a physical warehouse for furniture inventory, verify that the warehouse has the required construction, fire and environmental approvals before finalizing the bank mandate. Only after full registration should the corporate accounts be released from the escrow condition and connected to the intended payment rails such as Stripe and Affirm, subject to standard anti-money-laundering and know-your-business verification by the bank.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Corporate Registration or corporate register extract
Certified copy of the notarized Articles of Incorporation
Business registration application form and VAT questionnaire
Registered office lease agreement or ownership certificate
Identity card or passport of the representative director
Mail-order sales business report form
Proof of warehouse address and operating permits if a physical facility is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office rejects or suspends the business registration, correct the business code or address documentation and refile the application immediately. If the mail-order sales report is returned with missing attachments, the Company may resubmit through the local government online civil service system, and any administrative rejection may be appealed to the mayor or governor of the competent local government.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, Ministry of SMEs and Startups, the local municipal government in which any warehouse is located, the National Fire Agency, and the Korea Customs Service if the oversized furniture is imported
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Mail-Order Sales Business Report Certificate under the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce and, where a dedicated storage and distribution facility is maintained, the Warehouse and Distribution Facility Operation Approval under the Distribution Industry Development Act together with the Business Registration Certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, with technical support from the Korea Environment Corporation and the local municipal environmental department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration Exemption for this ISIC 4791 online retail and furniture distribution operation, because the activity is a non-manufacturing warehouse and logistics facility rather than a chemical, smelting, or disposal project. A Full Environmental Impact Assessment is not required where the total gross floor area of the distribution warehouse remains below the threshold for a city and county integrated development project under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act. If the warehouse is later expanded beyond the applicable threshold or if hazardous chemical storage is added, the operator must file a prior Environmental Impact Assessment or a small-scale environmental review.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater is generated. Sanitary wastewater from restrooms and break rooms must be discharged to a public sewer system and must satisfy the pre-treatment standards of the Sewerage Act; if on-site individual wastewater treatment is used, the final effluent must meet the Water Environment Conservation Act discharge standards, including biochemical oxygen demand of not more than 10 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand of not more than 10 mg/L, total suspended solids of not more than 10 mg/L and pH between 6.0 and 8.5. Stationary combustion equipment such as heating boilers must comply with the Clean Air Conservation Act emission limits. If packaging, paint touch-up or cleaning operations create volatile organic compound emissions, the operator must register with the local environmental authority when VOC release reaches ten tonnes or more per year and must install abatement equipment as required. All waste packaging, damaged furniture and wood scrap must be handled under the Waste Management Act and transported through licensed waste transfer stations with electronic manifest records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The warehouse and any retail distribution premise must obtain a fire safety completion inspection and, where applicable, a fire protection civil defense permit under the Fire Prevention, Installation, Maintenance and Safety Management Act and National Fire Agency regulations. The facility must be equipped with automatic fire detection and alarm systems, sprinklers where required by building area and storage height, fire doors, emergency lighting, exit signage and portable fire extinguishers, and the operator must appoint a fire safety manager when the gross floor area or employee count exceeds the statutory threshold. A civil defense shelter-use approval must be obtained if the building or site is designated in the local civil defense plan. The structural integrity of pallet racks and mezzanine storage used for oversized furniture must be certified by a licensed structural engineer, and the workplace must pass the occupational safety certification imposed by the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including manual lifting control measures, powered forklift inspection and licensing, rack load limitation signage, safety training, emergency response drills and prevention of musculoskeletal disorders.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating the electronic Home Tax Service (Hometax) portal at www.hometax.go.kr; import VAT and customs duties are administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) via the UNI-PASS system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) in South Korea: (1) incorporate the company with the Seoul District Court or competent local court and obtain a Certificate of Incorporation and corporate seal certificate; (2) apply for Business Registration with the local District Tax Office by submitting the articles of incorporation, certificate of incorporation, proof of Korean business premises, power of attorney, and certified foreign incorporation documents with apostille or consular legalization; (3) obtain the statutory 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which serves as both the corporate TIN and VAT registration number; (4) activate Hometax e-Tax Invoice access and, if exports are intended, register with Korea Customs Service for export trader status under UNI-PASS. If the foreign entity instead has no Korean fixed place of business but supplies electronic services or goods through a Korean marketplace, NTS requires non-resident simplified VAT registration through Hometax with a Korean tax representative, except where a marketplace withholding or platform VAT rule shifts the obligation; this is completed online with foreign incorporation evidence and the representative appointment deed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (the Republic of Korea has no check-the-box, classification, or hybrid mismatch election; a Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily taxed at entity level under the Corporate Tax Act, and anti-hybrid rules under the International Tax Adjustment Act apply mandatorily without elective treatment).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration threshold applies to a Korean-resident Chusik Hoesa; any person making taxable supplies of goods or services must register with the competent District Tax Office before commencing business, irrespective of turnover. A foreign non-resident supplier without a Korean fixed establishment selling electronic services to Korean consumers triggers simplified VAT registration when annual supplies exceed KRW 300,000,000; if the foreign supplier has a Korean fixed establishment or maintains local inventory, registration is unconditionally mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The National Tax Service mandates nationwide e-invoicing through the Hometax Electronic Tax Invoice (e-Tax Invoice) system. Every VAT-registered supplier issuing a tax invoice must transmit the invoice data to NTS no later than the same business day of issuance using the Hometax web service or API. B2C card transactions are automatically reported by acquirers, and cash sales to private individuals must be issued through the electronic cash receipt system when requested. The anti-fraud architecture uses centralised real-time invoice matching, reconciliation of customs declarations with VAT returns, and the national e-invoice network; no digital stamping or QR fiscal clearance is required for standard VAT invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 20 of the Korean Value Added Tax Act, zero-rate relief applies to (i) tangible goods exported from the Korean customs territory under a valid export declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service to a foreign customer or overseas consignee; (ii) services supplied from Korea to a place outside Korea or consumed overseas under the place-of-supply rules; and (iii) qualifying digital or information services supplied to non-resident customers, provided the Korean supplier is the exporter, receives the consideration in foreign exchange, and separately records the supplies as export zero-rated sales in the VAT return with supporting documentation retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration Confirmation issued by Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS electronic customs clearance system, constituting the governing Korean export shipment declaration
Bill of Lading (full ocean set), Air Waybill, or international cargo receipt showing goods loaded and destined to the foreign port or foreign consignee

Foreign Exchange Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, or a certificate of purchase of export bills evidencing repatriation of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Commercial invoice issued by the Korean exporter to the foreign buyer
Packing list, sales contract or purchase order, and any related insurance certificates corroborating the cross-border sale
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and KCS jointly conduct post-clearance audits of export transactions, electronically matching export declarations against VAT zero-rate returns, export invoices and bank foreign exchange receipts. For VAT zero-rating, export proceeds should be collected within a 180-day benchmark; if the proceeds are not repatriated in time without a bank-approved extension, the tax office may require additional evidence, reassess 10% VAT with interest, and claw back any refund already paid. Fraudulent or materially false export documentation (including fictitious exports, counterfeit foreign exchange certificates, undervaluation or sham contracts) triggers VAT reassessment, a surcharge of up to 40% of the unpaid tax, or up to 100% for intentional concealment, criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (imprisonment up to three years or fine), and retroactive withdrawal of refunds with statutory interest from the refund date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), as central bank and foreign-exchange information supervisor, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) which holds policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA); designated foreign exchange banks execute and report all regulated transactions under BOK oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains a liberalized yet strictly reported foreign exchange regime. Current account transactions, including export proceeds, overseas service fees, royalties, and remitted dividends from registered foreign-invested entities, are generally freely convertible into Korean won or foreign currency through a designated foreign exchange bank, provided the underlying trade or business transaction is evidenced and reported through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment, equity subscription, cross-border borrowings, and securities-related flows, are open but require prior filing or post-transaction reporting under FETA and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA). The Korean won is not a freely deliverable offshore currency; non-resident access is restricted to authorized settlement channels and onshore deliverable markets. Profit remittance is permitted for a Chusik Hoesa with valid foreign investment registration, but the bank will require corporate tax clearance, audited or certified financial statements, proof that the underlying equity was fully paid, and a statement confirming no unresolved foreign exchange violation. Export proceeds are not subject to mandatory conversion to Korean won, but they must be received domestically through a designated foreign exchange bank within statutory timelines. Overall convertibility is high for genuine current-account business flows, while capital-flow transactions are subject to substantive compliance review and documentary verification rather than hard currency rationing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under FETA and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, export proceeds must be collected and remitted to South Korea through a designated foreign exchange bank within six months from the date of export declaration or the date of service completion; an extension of up to six months may be applied for through the designated bank in cases of currency controls in the destination country, litigation, or documented trade disputes. The mandatory conversion ratio is zero percent: no statutory requirement exists to sell export proceeds to the Bank of Korea or to convert foreign currency receipts into Korean won. Retained proceeds may be held in the exporter's foreign currency account. However, for each receipt, the exporter must file a receipt-of-export-proceeds report through the bank, and if the full proceeds are not received by the deadline, a non-receipt or deferred-receipt report must be submitted. Any conversion into KRW is executed at the prevailing market exchange rate and does not require central bank approval, but it must be recorded with the correct foreign exchange transaction purpose code.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital e-money institutions and non-bank EMIs are not viable as the primary treasury or settlement rail for a South Korean-domiciled Chusik Hoesa. South Korean banking law and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act reserve deposit-taking and foreign-exchange settlement functions to licensed banks and registered electronic financial business operators. A foreign EMI cannot legally open a native Korean account in the entity's name or issue an IBAN for inward foreign direct investment, export collection, or trade settlement. Fintech players such as Stripe and Affirm may be used only as upstream customer-facing payment gateways and point-of-sale credit providers, with settlement funds swept into a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank operating account. Any offshore EMI claim to act as a settlement bank for Korean trade flows is legally barred; all regulated cross-border transaction reporting must be performed by a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory for the legal representative or an in-country responsible director when opening corporate bank accounts for a newly incorporated Chusik Hoesa. Korean Tier-1 banks do not permit a fully remote consular proxy opening; at minimum, one authorized executive or the statutory representative director must appear at a domestic branch for identity verification, execution of bank signature cards, and anti-money-laundering interview. Remote overseas notarized power of attorney may be accepted only to supplement the in-person opening, not to replace it. The bank will require the corporate registry certificate (registered business certificate), articles of incorporation, shareholder register, resolution of the board of directors authorizing account opening and foreign exchange transactions, UBO declaration, passports/government IDs of all directors and authorized signatories, proof of registered address, and a corporate seal certificate. In practice, for a non-resident-controlled entity, bankers will also request an in-person video interview and written confirmation that the economic settlor and beneficial owner are not subject to sanctions or adverse media.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident controller structure with opaque beneficial ownership or a physical-person shareholder outside Korea without verified source of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified extract from the Korean registry for the Chusik Hoesa, full shareholder ledger, personal bank reference letters, certified passports of all shareholders and directors, source-of-wealth documentation such as tax returns, audited financial statements or asset records, corporate structure chart up to ultimate beneficial owners, and a board resolution confirming UBO attestations. All non-Korean documents must be notarized, apostilled where applicable, and translated into Korean by a certified translator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual inbound capital injection pattern for an e-commerce entity, such as large equity funding prior to any purchase orders or supplier contracts, creating a risk of money-laundering or round-tripping
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign investment report filed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act with the designated foreign exchange bank, capital introduction schedule, investor bank confirmation traceable through SWIFT MT103 messages, business plan and financial projections, executed supplier agreements, e-commerce platform incorporation documents, and evidence of operational substance such as warehousing or logistics contracts in the oversized furniture sector.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade red flags involving high-value oversized home-furniture transactions, including mismatches between declared invoices, customs values, and payment currency for trade settlements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete digital trade file: purchase orders, commercial invoices, packing lists with volumetric and weight data, bills of lading or airway bills, customs import/export declarations, freight forwarder contracts, insurance certificates, tax invoices, proof of third-party payment authorization, and periodic reconciliation of amounts paid against customs entries. The bank should also receive an independent accountant's letter confirming revenue recognition for each export or import batch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential abuse of payment gateway and BNPL settlement flows, such as refund splitting, chargeback cycling, or use of the corporate account as a pass-through for unexplained retail settlements from multiple countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe and Affirm merchant settlement reports for at least the trailing six months, chargeback and refund registers, clearing journal from the payment processor into the South Korean operating account, internal control policies covering refunds and dispute handling, customer identification procedures, order analytics, logistics proof for delivered oversized furniture, and a letter from the external auditor confirming no shell activity or unrelated third-party pass-through funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital for the Chusik Hoesa must be routed as follows: the non-resident shareholder first files a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act at a designated foreign exchange bank or KOTRA, obtains foreign investor registration, then sends a SWIFT MT103 wire to the Korean company's capital escrow account. The remittance must clearly state the foreign exchange purpose code for direct investment or equity acquisition, referencing the foreign investment report number and the target company name. Upon receipt, the domestic bank verifies the remitter, beneficiary, amount, and purpose code against the approved foreign investment report. Funds are then recorded in FEIS as inward foreign direct investment; the bank issues a foreign investment certificate or capital verification statement after confirming that the subscription price has been fully settled. No inward remittance can be treated as paid-in capital without this verification, and any conversion into Korean won must be executed at the market rate through the designated foreign exchange bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the import side of the oversized home-furniture business, payments to overseas furniture manufacturers should be made via SWIFT MT103 direct transfer with a precise trade-related purpose code, matching the import declaration, supplier pro-forma invoice, and bill of lading. For large purchase orders, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued by the Korean bank is preferable; usance LC terms may be used for working capital breathing room. Documentary collections D/P and D/A are permitted only for established and verified counterparties. For export-side operations, if the Korean entity sells oversized goods abroad, the buyer's remittance must be received through the designated foreign exchange bank and reported as export proceeds. The bank will clear the KRW leg through BOK-Wire for domestic payments and through the bank's overseas correspondent network in USD/EUR/CNY for cross-border transfers; all settlement messages must cite the underlying contract, invoice, customs declaration, and logistics reference to satisfy Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts with a designated foreign exchange bank, permitted only where there is a genuine trade receivable or payable evidenced by an export/import declaration, sales contract, or LC supporting the tenor and notional amount
FX swaps between KRW and USD/EUR/CNY for matching liquidity inflows from export receipts and liquidity outflows to overseas suppliers, subject to real-demand and reporting rules
Plain vanilla currency options for hedging freight, customs, and logistics costs paid to foreign carriers, covering recognized procurement exposures

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps where permitted for a Chusik Hoesa with external borrowing from a foreign bank, subject to prior foreign exchange reporting and confirmation that the swap is ancillary to the underlying loan

Non-deliverable forwards are not recommended as the primary onshore hedge for a domestic Korean entity; they are generally offshore-market instruments for non-resident counterparties and would not satisfy the real-demand underwriting requirement for the Company's designated bank relationship

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year companies, by 31 March. One-month extension to 30 April available when filing through a certified tax agent with a prepayment; additional extensions limited to circumstances under Framework Act on National Taxes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or under-report triggers a 10-20% accuracy penalty on unpaid national tax plus 0.022% daily delinquent surcharge; non-filing permits the NTS to issue a forced official assessment; prolonged dormancy of 5 consecutive years can lead to court-ordered dissolution under Article 176 of the Korean Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge Return (Special Local Tax on Corporate Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Metropolitan City / Do / Gu Local Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as national corporate income tax deadline: within 3 months of fiscal year-end, repectively by 31 March for calendar-year financial periods.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10-20% of underpaid local tax, daily delinquency surcharge of 0.022%, and enforced collection through seizure of corporate assets; continued default can trigger administrative measures by the local government.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholders' Annual General Meeting Minutes and Financial Statement Approval Record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing; documents stored at the registered head office and made available to shareholders; copy attached to the corporate income tax return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual General Meeting must be held within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year; financial statements must be approved by the AGM before filing the tax return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM or preserve the approved minutes violates the Korean Commercial Act; negligent directors may become jointly and severally liable; the NTS may deem financial statements unapproved and impose document execution penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report (when audit threshold triggered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) as an attachment to the annual corporate income tax return; audit firm retains a signed report.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted to NTS together with the corporate income tax return within 3 months of fiscal year-end (extension as permitted for the tax return).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission of a mandatory external audit or failure to attach the report constitutes a violation of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; fines up to KRW 300 million and imprisonment of company directors can be imposed, and the tax return is treated as defective causing additional tax penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Enterprise Annual Report (if a non-resident shareholder holds 10% or more)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) / Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the designated foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of each fiscal year under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 1 million and possible revocation of foreign-investment tax reduction benefits; repeat violations may trigger an order to correct or, in egregious cases, investment cancellation procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner / Controlling Shareholder Disclosure in Annual Corporate Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted annually with the corporate income tax return; any shareholding transfer or change of controlling shareholder that affects tax record must be reported within 30 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False, incomplete, or delayed disclosure triggers penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes: a fine up to 5% of the relevant tax base amount, plus daily interest; continued non-disclosure may trigger tax reassessment and criminal referral.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (Law No. 17564, as amended), an independent certified CPA audit is mandatory for a Chusik Hoesa if: (a) total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 8.57 million at 1,400 KRW/USD) at the fiscal year-end; (b) the company is listed on a Korean securities exchange; (c) the company is engaged in banking, insurance, financial investment, or other public-interest industries as specifically designated by Korean law; (d) the company's annual revenue is KRW 100 billion or more (approximately USD 71.4 million) under certain industry-specific rules; or (e) shareholders owning at least 3% of the issued shares request an external audit in accordance with the statutory procedure. This e-commerce entity (ISIC 4791, home furniture online retail) is not automatically exempt merely because it is private; it must test total assets at each year-end once the KRW 12 billion asset threshold is crossed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are mandatory for entities subject to external audit; non-public, non-audited companies may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP, i.e. the General Corporate Accounting Standards) in their separate financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation in the corporate register. However, the corporate tax return requires annual disclosure of the ultimate beneficial owner and any controlling shareholder; any share transfer recorded in the Register of Members must be reflected in the company's shareholder ledger and reported to the NTS within a 30-day statutory reporting window when the transfer affects tax registration obligations. Foreign investors acquiring 10% or more of a Chusik Hoesa must report the acquisition to MOTIE within 20 days and file an annual foreign investment enterprise report within 90 days after each fiscal year-end.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (and Register of Statutory Auditors if applicable)
Register of Secured Obligations/Mortgage charges affecting the company's assets
Minute Book (AGM and Board of Directors meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000 - USD 30,000 per annum for a statutory audit by an independent licensed CPA firm

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive national corporate income tax rate: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion. A 10% local income tax surcharge applies on the national corporate tax, raising aggregate headline rates to approximately 9.9%, 20.9%, 23.1%, and 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: South Korea does not operate a general patent box. Available incentives include Foreign Investment Promotion Act tax holidays and reductions for qualifying advanced-technology foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones (100% exemption for three years and 50% for two years in eligible cases), Special Tax Treatment Control Act credits for SME R&D investment, job creation, and facility investment, and standard depreciation or temporary investment tax incentives. The online oversized-furniture retail business under ISIC 4791 has no bespoke e-commerce tax holiday and therefore uses ordinary taxable income rules.
